plan: 2 Samuel 24:1-9; 1 Chronicles 21:1-6; 2 Samuel 24:10-17; 1 Chronicles 21:7-17; 2 Samuel 24:18-25; 1 Chronicles 21:18–22:1; 1 Chronicles 22:2-19

readings.title: Dawiḏ Numbers the People
readings.subtitle: The Census Commanded
readings.text: [2 Samuel 24:1] And again the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Yisra’ěl, and <dn>He</dn> moved <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ against them to say, <dq>“Go, number <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl and <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏah.”</dq> [2] And the sovereign said to Yo’aḇ the commander of the army who was with him, “Go now, throughout all the tribes of Yisra’ěl, from Dan to Be’ěrsheḇa, and register <dn>את</dn> the people, so that I know <dn>את</dn> the number of the people.” [3] And Yo’aḇ said to the sovereign, “Now may <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> add to the people a hundred times more than there are, and let the eyes of my master the sovereign see it. But why does my master the sovereign delight in this matter?” [4] But the word of the sovereign was strict against Yo’aḇ and against the commanders of the army. And Yo’aḇ and the commanders of the army went out from the presence of the sovereign to register <dn>את</dn> the people of Yisra’ěl. [5] And they passed over the Yarděn and camped in Aro‛ěr, on the right side of the town which is in the midst of the wadi of Gaḏ, and toward Ya‛zěr, [6] and came to Gil‛aḏ and to the land of Taḥtim Hoḏshi, and they came to Dan Ya‛an and around to Tsiḏon, [7] and came to the stronghold of Tsor, and to all the cities of the Ḥiwwites and the Kena‛anites. And they went out to South Yehuḏah, as far as Be’ěrsheḇa. [8] And they went through all the land, and came to Yerushalayim at the end of nine months and twenty days. [9] And Yo’aḇ gave <dn>את</dn> the number of the registration of the people to the sovereign. And there were in Yisra’ěl eight hundred thousand brave men who drew the sword, and the men of Yehuḏah were five hundred thousand men.

readings.title: Satan Stands Against Yisra’ěl
readings.subtitle: The Chronicler's Account of the Census
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 21:1] And Satan stood up against Yisra’ěl, and moved <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ to number <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl. [2] So Dawiḏ said to Yo’aḇ and to the leaders of the people, “Go, number <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from Be’ěrsheḇa to Dan, and bring <dn>את</dn> the number of them to me so that I know it.” [3] And Yo’aḇ answered, “May <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> make <dn>His</dn> people a hundred times more than they are. My master the sovereign, are they not all my master’s servants? Why does my master seek this? Why should he be a cause of guilt in Yisra’ěl?” [4] But the word of the sovereign was strict against Yo’aḇ. So Yo’aḇ left and went throughout all Yisra’ěl and came to Yerushalayim. [5] And Yo’aḇ gave <dn>את</dn> the number of the registration of the people to Dawiḏ. And all Yisra’ěl were one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and Yehuḏah was four hundred and seventy thousand men who drew the sword. [6] But Lěwi and Binyamin he did not register among them, for the word of the sovereign was disgusting to Yo’aḇ.

readings.title: The Consequence of Pride
readings.subtitle: Three Choices of Judgment
readings.text: [2 Samuel 24:10] And the heart of Dawiḏ smote him after he had numbered <dn>את</dn> the people. And Dawiḏ said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “I have sinned greatly in what I have done. And now, I pray, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, take away <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of <dn>Your</dn> servant, for I have done very foolishly.” [11] And Dawiḏ rose up in the morning, and the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to the prophet Gaḏ, the seer of Dawiḏ, saying, [12] <dq>“Go, and you shall speak to Dawiḏ, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “<dn>I</dn> am lifting up to you three choices, choose one of them for <dn>Me</dn> to do to you.” ’ ”</dq> [13] So Gaḏ came to Dawiḏ and informed him. And he said to him, “Should seven years of scarcity of food come to you in your land? Or would you flee three months before your enemies, while they pursue you? Or should there be three days’ plague in your land? Now know and see what answer I take back to <dn>Him</dn> who sent me.” [14] And Dawiḏ said to Gaḏ, “I am in great distress. Please let us fall into the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>His</dn> compassions are great, but do not let me fall into the hand of man.” [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent a plague upon Yisra’ěl from the morning till the appointed time, and from Dan to Be’ěrsheḇa seventy thousand men of the people died. [16] And the messenger stretched out <dn>His</dn> hand over Yerushalayim to destroy it, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> relented concerning the evil, and said to the messenger who was destroying the people, <dq>“It is enough, now stay your hand.”</dq> And the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was by the threshing-floor of Arawnah the Yeḇusite. [17] And Dawiḏ spoke to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> when he saw <dn>את</dn> the messenger who was smiting the people, and he said, “See, I have sinned, and I have done perversely. But these sheep, what have they done? Let <dn>Your</dn> hand, I pray, be against me and against my father’s house.”

readings.title: The Sword of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The Messenger at the Threshing-Floor
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 21:7] And this matter was evil in the eyes of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> smote <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl. [8] And Dawiḏ said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “I have sinned greatly, in that I have done <dn>את</dn> this matter. But now, I pray, remove <dn>את</dn> the crookedness of <dn>Your</dn> servant, for I have done very foolishly.” [9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Gaḏ, the seer of Dawiḏ, saying, [10] <dq>“Go, and you shall speak to Dawiḏ, saying, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “<dn>I</dn> hold out to you three choices, choose one of them for <dn>Me</dn> to do to you.” ’ ”</dq> [11] So Gaḏ came to Dawiḏ and said to him, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Choose for yourself:</dq> [12] <dq>either three years of scarcity of food, or three months to be defeated by your foes with the sword of your enemies overtaking you, or else for three days the sword of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – the plague in the land, with the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> destroying throughout all the borders of Yisra’ěl.’</dq> And now, see what answer I take back to <dn>Him</dn> who sent me.” [13] And Dawiḏ said to Gaḏ, “I am in great distress. Please let me fall into the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>His</dn> compassions are very great, but do not let me fall into the hand of man.” [14] So <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent a plague upon Yisra’ěl, and seventy thousand men of Yisra’ěl fell. [15] And <dn>Elohim</dn> sent a messenger to Yerushalayim to destroy it. And as he was destroying, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> looked and relented concerning the evil, and said to the messenger who was destroying, <dq>“It is enough, now stay your hand.”</dq> And the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> stood by the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite. [16] And Dawiḏ lifted up <dn>את</dn> his eyes and saw <dn>את</dn> the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> standing between the earth and the heavens, having in his hand a drawn sword stretched out over Yerushalayim. And Dawiḏ and the elders, covered with sackcloth, fell on their faces. [17] And Dawiḏ said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Was it not I who commanded <dn>את</dn> the people to be numbered? And I am the one who has sinned and done very evilly, but these sheep, what have they done? O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, let <dn>Your</dn> hand, I pray, be against me and against my father’s house, but not against <dn>Your</dn> people, to be plagued.”

readings.title: A Price Paid for Peace
readings.subtitle: Dawiḏ Purchases the Threshing-Floor
readings.text: [2 Samuel 24:18] And Gaḏ came that day to Dawiḏ and said to him, “Go up, raise an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the threshing-floor of Arawnah the Yeḇusite.” [19] And Dawiḏ, according to the word of Gaḏ, went up as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded. [20] And Arawnah looked and saw <dn>את</dn> the sovereign and <dn>את</dn> his servants coming toward him. And Arawnah went out and bowed before the sovereign with his face to the ground. [21] And Arawnah said, “Why has my master the sovereign come to his servant?” And Dawiḏ said, “To buy <dn>את</dn> the threshing-floor from you, to build an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, so that the plague is withdrawn from the people.” [22] And Arawnah said to Dawiḏ, “Let my master the sovereign take and offer up what is good in his eyes. See, here are cattle for ascending offerings, and threshing implements and the yokes of the cattle for wood. [23] “All these, O sovereign, Arawnah has given to the sovereign.” And Arawnah said to the sovereign, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> accept you!” [24] And the sovereign said to Arawnah, “No, let me buy it from you for a price, for certain. I am not offering ascending offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn> without cost.” So Dawiḏ bought <dn>את</dn> the threshing-floor and <dn>את</dn> the cattle for fifty sheqels of silver. [25] And Dawiḏ built an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> there, and offered ascending offerings and peace offerings. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered the prayers for the land, and the plague was withdrawn from Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Fire from the Heavens
readings.subtitle: The Foundation of the Future Temple
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 21:18] And the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Gaḏ to say to Dawiḏ that Dawiḏ should go and raise an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite. [19] And Dawiḏ went up at the word of Gaḏ, which he had spoken in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [20] And Ornan turned and saw <dn>את</dn> the messenger. And his four sons with him hid themselves, but Ornan continued threshing wheat. [21] And Dawiḏ came to Ornan, and Ornan looked and saw <dn>את</dn> Dawiḏ, and he went out from the threshing-floor, and bowed before Dawiḏ with his face to the ground. [22] And Dawiḏ said to Ornan, “Give me <dn>את</dn> the place of this threshing-floor, to build an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on it. Give it to me for the full price, so that the plague is withdrawn from the people.” [23] And Ornan said to Dawiḏ, “Take it to yourself, and let my master the sovereign do what is good in his eyes. See, I shall give the cattle for ascending offerings, and the threshing implements for wood, and the wheat for the grain offering – I give it all.” [24] And Sovereign Dawiḏ said to Ornan, “No, but I shall certainly buy it for the full price, for I do not take <dn>את</dn> what is yours for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor offer ascending offerings without cost.” [25] So Dawiḏ gave Ornan six hundred sheqels of gold by weight for the place. [26] And Dawiḏ built an altar to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> there, and offered ascending offerings and peace offerings, and called on <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>He</dn> answered him from the heavens by fire on the altar of ascending offering. [27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded the messenger, and he returned his sword to its sheath. [28] At that time, when Dawiḏ saw that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had answered him on the threshing-floor of Ornan the Yeḇusite, he slaughtered there. [29] For the Dwelling Place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the altar of the ascending offering, which Mosheh had made in the wilderness, were at that time at the high place in Giḇ‛on. [30] But Dawiḏ was unable to go before it to inquire of <dn>Elohim</dn>, for he was afraid of the sword of the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [1 Chronicles 22:1] And Dawiḏ said, “This is the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and this is the altar of ascending offering for Yisra’ěl.”

readings.title: A Legacy of Preparation
readings.subtitle: Dawiḏ Commissions Shelomoh to Build the House
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 22:2] And Dawiḏ commanded to gather <dn>את</dn> the aliens who were in the land of Yisra’ěl. And he appointed stonecutters to hew cut stones to build the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [3] And Dawiḏ prepared iron in large amounts for the nails of the doors of the gates and for the joints, and bronze in large amounts beyond weighing, [4] and cedar trees innumerable, for the Tsiḏonians and those from Tsor brought large amounts of cedar wood to Dawiḏ. [5] And Dawiḏ said, “Shelomoh my son is young and tender, and the house to be built for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is to be exceedingly great, for a name and for an esteem throughout all lands. Let me now prepare for it.” So Dawiḏ prepared large amounts before his death. [6] And he called for Shelomoh his son, and commanded him to build a house for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl. [7] And Dawiḏ said to Shelomoh, “My son, as for me, it has been in my heart to build a house to the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, [8] but the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying, <dq>‘You have shed much blood and have fought great battles. You are not to build a house for <dn>My</dn> Name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in <dn>My</dn> presence.</dq> [9] <dq>‘See, a son is to be born to you, who is a man of rest. And <dn>I</dn> shall give him rest from all his enemies all around, for Shelomoh is his name, and peace and quiet <dn>I</dn> give to Yisra’ěl in his days.</dq> [10] <dq>‘He does build a house for <dn>My</dn> Name, and he is to be <dn>My</dn> son, and <dn>I</dn> am his <dn>Father</dn>. And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the throne of his reign over Yisra’ěl forever.’</dq> [11] “Now, my son, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be with you. And you shall prosper, and build <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> has said to you. [12] “Only, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> give you wisdom and understanding, and give you charge concerning Yisra’ěl, to guard <dn>את</dn> the Torah of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [13] “Then you shall prosper, if you guard to do <dn>את</dn> the laws and <dn>את</dn> the right-rulings with which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh concerning Yisra’ěl. Be strong and courageous, do not fear nor be dismayed. [14] “And see, in my trouble I have prepared for the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> one hundred thousand talents of gold and one million talents of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, for it is so much. And I have prepared timber and stone, and you should add to them. [15] “And with you are many workmen, stonecutters and hewers of stone and timber, and all types of skilled men for every kind of work. [16] “Of gold and silver and bronze and iron there is no limit. Arise and begin, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be with you.” [17] And Dawiḏ commanded all the leaders of Yisra’ěl to help Shelomoh his son, saying, [18] “Is not <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with you? And has <dn>He</dn> not given you rest on every side? For <dn>He</dn> has given <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has been subdued before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and before <dn>His</dn> people. [19] “Now, give your heart and your being to seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. And arise and build <dn>את</dn> the set-apart place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, to bring <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the set-apart vessels of <dn>Elohim</dn> into the house that is to be built for the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
